alignments.note: Postpositive δέ rendered by the clause-initial But.
Adverb νῦν → now.
Inflected verb takes its supplied subject pronoun under rules 7 and 9; head on the lexical verb desire.

Anarthrous substantival comparative adjective: no article competes, so the supplied determiner a and the supplied generic noun country are rule 7 helpers on the adjective (rules 17, 51, 102's anarthrous contrast). Head on better, the word glossing κρείττων.
Demonstrative τοῦτ' → that.
Expressed copula ἔστιν → is; rule 53 does not arise, the verb being expressed.
Anarthrous substantival adjective with supplied indefinite determiner as a rule 7 helper (rule 51's anarthrous clause); head on heavenly.
διό → wherefore.
Ordinary negative οὐκ → not; no negative indefinite follows, so rules 41 and 59 do not arise.

Finite verb with its copular auxiliary; rule 17 heads on the lexical predicate ashamed rather than on is. The English of is the predicate's own government rather than a case preposition: the object is accusative, which English marks with no preposition, and no Greek preposition stands, so under rule 36's reasoning it rides with the verb as after does at 11.6 and 11.14, for at 11.10 and through at 11.29. Discontinuous under rule 15, the negative standing between. Reading of as a rule 21 case helper on the pronoun is the competing analysis and was the accepted one; the chapter's other four units of this construction decided it.
Accusative object; the pronoun stands bare, the supplied of belonging to the English predicate ashamed of, as him stands bare after seek after at 11.6.
Article governing the subject θεός; the ASV writes a bare God with no determiner, so the article realizes nothing (rule 23).
Subject θεός → God (t013), the God of the main clause.
Predicate θεός of the infinitival clause → the second God (t023); the possessive their belongs to αὐτῶν under rule 20, so the noun stands bare.
Passive infinitive; no conjunction governs the clause, so the infinitival to and the copular be are rule 7/9 helpers on the verb (rules 40, 61). Head on called.
Genitive pronoun αὐτῶν rendered by the possessive their (rule 20); no article stands with the predicate noun in any case.
Postpositive γάρ rendered by the clause-initial for.
Aorist with supplied subject and perfect auxiliary as rule 9 helpers; head on the lexical verb prepared.

Dative pronoun rendered for them, the supplied preposition realizing the case and riding with the pronoun (rules 7, 21). Head on them. This is the contrast with s011: a case preposition stays with the noun, a predicate's governed preposition with the verb.
Anarthrous πόλιν with its supplied indefinite determiner as a rule 7 helper (rule 51's anarthrous clause); head on city.

review_notes: Only the boundary between s010 and s011 changes; every other unit, head and note is as the verse pass returned it.

The dative αὐτοῖς at s019 keeps its supplied for, because there the preposition does realize a case and rides with the pronoun under rules 7 and 21. The two pronouns of this verse are therefore treated differently on purpose, and the difference is the case, which is what convention 1 records.
s010's unit is discontinuous under rule 15, the negative t015 standing between is and ashamed of; the head stays on the lexical predicate ashamed under rule 17.
Every s### and t### appears exactly once and each head is a member of its own array: 20 source ids and 31 target ids partitioned.
